Destitute

/dih-STIH-toot/ — rhymes with brute · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Destitute describes someone who has no money or resources at all, left with nothing to live on.

The flood left dozens of families destitute, without homes or savings.

Worked Example

After the factory closure and eviction, the elderly couple became destitute, sleeping in their car with only the clothes they wore.

Destitute captures the complete and total lack of resources — not just poor or struggling, but left with absolutely nothing at all. This precision conveys the desperation and extremity that the word 'poor' alone could never express.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

penniless: Penniless means having no money at all — the wallet and the bank account are empty. Destitute goes wider: no money and no resources of any kind, nothing to live on. A traveler can be penniless for a weekend; a destitute family has lost home, savings, and every means of survival.

bankrupt: Bankrupt is a legal and financial word: a person or company officially unable to pay its debts. A bankrupt business owner may still keep a house and a car while the paperwork is settled. Destitute describes bare human need — left with no money or resources at all, nothing to live on.

needy: Needy is the everyday word for people who lack basic necessities and require help — food drives collect for needy families. Destitute is far more extreme and more formal: it means stripped of everything, with nothing at all to live on, the state a disaster can leave behind.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

wealthy: having plenty of money and possessions

prosperous: financially successful and thriving in life

Where it sits · how little money someone has left — struggling → poor → impoverished → destitute

struggling vs. destitute: Struggling is much weaker than destitute: a struggling family has trouble paying its bills, while a destitute one has nothing left to pay with at all.

poor vs. destitute: Poor is weaker than destitute — poor means having very little money, while destitute means having no money or resources whatsoever.

impoverished vs. destitute: Impoverished comes close, but destitute is stronger still: impoverished people have been drained into poverty, while destitute people are left with absolutely nothing to live on.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: away, down (Latin)

Root — stitut (from statuere)

Root — stitut (from statuere): to set, place, cause to stand (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin destituere meant 'to forsake or abandon' — literally to set (statuere) someone away or down (de-) and leave them standing alone. A destitute person has been left standing with nothing: no money and no resources at all.

Use the root in a new word: substitute

Use the root in a new word: substitute: A substitute teacher is placed in the regular teacher's spot for the day — the same Latin root statuere, 'to place,' that sits inside destitute.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Destitute is a powerful, formal word describing absolute deprivation — used in serious contexts like poverty, refugee situations, or disaster aftermath. For everyday financial struggle, use 'poor' or 'struggling.'
